title: Mus'ab the teacher
hookLine: Mus'ab ibn Umayr is sent to teach the Qur'an in Yathrib, and many believe

cards: The twelve are heading home with a promise and a problem. They believe, but who will teach them? Who will recite the Qur'an to their families, lead their prayer, answer the questions that come up at dinner?
So the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, sends someone with them. Not a clan elder. Mus'ab ibn Umayr, a Meccan who, tradition says, had left a comfortable life behind for this faith.
In Yathrib, Ibn Ishaq says, people came to call him simply the reciter. Today: al-Muqri.

teach.b: Mus'ab stays with a man of Yathrib, As'ad ibn Zurara, and the two go out into the gardens and neighborhoods, reciting. Not everyone is pleased.

One day, Ibn Ishaq says, a clan leader, Usayd ibn Hudayr, comes striding toward them with his spear, angry. What have you come here for, to make fools of our weak ones? Leave us, if you value your life.

teach.h: WILL YOU NOT SIT AND LISTEN?
teach.b: He says, roughly: will you not sit down and listen? If you like what you hear, accept it.

teach.h: IF YOU DISLIKE IT, WE STOP.
teach.b: If you dislike it, we'll keep away from what you dislike. Usayd thinks that's fair. He plants his spear in the ground and sits.
Mus'ab recites, and the story says that before Usayd had spoken a word, they could see the change in his face. He asks what a person does to enter this faith.
Then Usayd sends a greater leader, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, who comes in just as angry, and the same thing happens: an invitation to sit, a recitation, a changed face.

Sa'd goes back to his own clan, Ibn Ishaq says, and asks how they regard him. When they answer with respect, he tells them he won't speak to them until they believe. Tradition says that by evening, his clan had.
That's the whole method in the story: sit down, listen, you are free to say no.
The teacher puts the words in front of people, and steps back.

how: Muslims remember Mus'ab ibn Umayr as the teacher sent to Yathrib before the hijra, and his invitation to sit and listen is often retold when people talk about how to share the faith gently.

games.q: you're Mus'ab. an angry clan leader comes at you with a spear and tells you to leave. what do you say?
o: you have no right to stop me.
will you sit down and listen?
games.why: he invited him to sit and listen, and promised to stop if he disliked it. Usayd planted his spear and sat.

practice: Choose a short line you know by heart. If you're Muslim, it might be from a short surah: in Pickthall's old translation, the hundred and twelfth opens: Say: He is Allah, the One!
If not, any line that matters to you will do; say it once, quietly, the way Mus'ab offered his: here it is, take it or leave it.

wordCard.voice: Al-Muqri, the reciter. Mus'ab ibn Umayr's name in Yathrib, where he recited the Qur'an to anyone who would sit, and left them free to say no. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the reciter, the one who teaches the Qur'an aloud; Mus'ab's name in Yathrib.

carryVoice: Your line: the first teacher. He recited, and then he stepped back. That's day seven hundred sixty.

sources.ref: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (Mus'ab sent with the men of the first Aqaba; called the reciter; stays with As'ad ibn Zurara; Usayd ibn Hudayr and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh accept Islam; Sa'd's clan)
